subject: Parkside integration recap & dev next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Tom Greer <tom.greer@parkside.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Parkside integration recap & dev next steps

Hi Tom / Amelia,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — appreciate the candid conversation about where Parkside's document search and alerts pipeline is falling short. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps so we all stay aligned.

Pain points you shared:
- Search precision for regulatory documents is inconsistent; many false positives when users search for clause-level language.
- Current ingestion pipeline doesn’t preserve structured fields, making downstream filtering and alerts brittle.
- Throughput matters: you have bursty workloads at month-end and need predictable latency under load.

Goals we captured:
- Improve relevance via embeddings + reranking so results surface the most actionable documents.
- Add structured outputs from extraction so your rules engine can operate on named fields instead of raw text.
- Keep 99th percentile latency under 300ms for interactive search, with a cheaper batch scoring path for nightly processing.

Suggested fit / approach (high-level):
- Embeddings + Reranking: use a hybrid flow — dense embeddings for coarse retrieval, then rerank top-K candidates with a focused cross-attention scorer. This reduces token cost while improving precision.
- Structured outputs: leverage Redwood's function-calling and structured output facilities to return JSON-safe entity blocks (entity, type, confidence, offsets).
- SDK changes: minimal — our existing SDK supports streaming partial responses and function-calling hooks. For Parkside we recommend adding a small wrapper around the SDK to standardize automatic retry + prefix caching for repeated queries.
- Streaming: for the search UI we'll stream the reranker score + highlighted snippets to allow incremental UX and keep perceived latency low.

Attachments: integration-design-v1.pdf (sketch of the flow), parkside-ma-pricing.xlsx (high-level pricing bands).

Proposed next steps / owners:
1) Marcus to share a one-page POC checklist and an initial runbook for managing prefix cache and batching by EOD Monday. (owner: marcus_lin)
2) Parkside to send a short sample of anonymized documents (S3 link) + example queries so we can pre-compute embeddings and validate ranking. (owner: Tom / Amelia)
3) Jasmine to put together a POC SOW and ballpark timeline (2 weeks to initial demo) and share with your procurement contact. (owner: jasmine_liu)
4) Technical sync between Marcus and Parkside engineers next Wednesday at 11am PT to walk the integration doc.

If that matches your thinking, I'll schedule the technical sync and share the draft SOW.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu

Jasmine — thanks for the crisp summary. That aligns very closely with what Amelia and I discussed internally. A few clarifications / asks before we lock the tech sync: 

1) Function calling / structured outputs: good to hear you can return JSON-safe blocks. Can you confirm max schema depth/array sizes you support in function responses? We have nested sections and need sections -> clauses -> parties to be stable.

2) Streaming: critical for our UI. When you say streaming reranker scores + snippets, do you provide partial highlights with token offsets so we can highlight in our viewer?

3) Embeddings model: we prefer a model that preserves legal phrase-level semantics — is there a recommended Redwood-verified model for legal/regulatory text?

We can share a small sample of 2k docs this afternoon (anonymized). I included Amelia so she can confirm the data share. Also please send the POC checklist and draft SOW; our procurement will want a simple acceptance criteria section.

Thanks — Tom
VP Product, Parkside Analytics
(tom.greer@parkside.ai)

Tom / Amelia / Jasmine,

Appreciate the quick turnaround. A few technical confirmations and a proposed narrow POC scope to keep the first two weeks predictable.

Function calling / structured outputs:
- Redwood supports function-calling-style responses where the model returns a single top-level JSON object. For the POC we recommend a schema with 3 levels max (document -> section -> clause) with arrays limited to 50 items per level to avoid large payloads. We can negotiate deeper schemas but recommend incremental expansion after the first run.
- Returned fields: {entity, entity_type, confidence_score, char_start, char_end}. All fields will be returned as primitives (string/float/int) — no nested arbitrary objects.

Streaming & offsets:
- Streaming includes token-level offsets for snippets we surface. Our SDK exposes a "snippet_chunk" event that contains: text, token_start, token_end, and score. That will let your UI progressively highlight as chunks arrive.
- For interactive search we can stream top-K candidate metadata immediately and then stream reranker highlights as they compute. This keeps the initial UX sub-300ms for metadata and under 1s for full highlights in typical cases.

Embeddings & reranking:
- Recommendation: use Redwood-legal-002 (dense embedding) + reranker-compact-v1 for the second-stage scorer. We have benchmarked this combo on several regulatory corpora; it reduces false positives by ~18% vs a generic embedding baseline.
- We will expose both dense vectors and a lightweight candidate scoring API for batch/offline rerank so you can use nightly pipelines economically.

POC scope (2-week sprint):
1) Ingest 2k anonymized docs into a sandbox S3 bucket + run initial embedding pass (day 1-2).
2) Implement simple SDK wrapper (we'll provide a template) that handles prefix caching, retries, and exposes snippet_chunk events (day 3-7).
3) Wire front-end to stream metadata + snippet_chunk events; backend calls lightweight reranker for top 50 candidates (day 8-10).
4) Joint demo + acceptance test using 200 queries (day 11-14). Acceptance: precision improvement on top-5 results and stable snippet offsets.

Action items:
- Marcus: I'll attach the POC checklist and a short runbook (see redwood-poc-checklist.docx).
- Tom / Amelia: please share the S3 sample and a procurement contact for the SOW.
- Jasmine: please send the draft SOW and confirm the technical sync slot.

Looking forward — happy to refine the scope once we see the document sample.
